MoneyMapperThe story behind your score

One number for your entire financial health.

Your Financial Fitness Score doesn't appear out of thin air. Let's follow one person's story to see how it really comes together.

Inspired by real-life money situations
The beginning

Meet Aarav

Aarav is 28. He has a good job, a salary that lands every month, and one question that keeps him up at night: "Am I actually okay financially, or do I just look okay?"

His friends say everything's fine. His bank balance says nothing at all. So Aarav opens MoneyMapper, and the app looks at his entire financial life through five pillars.

Every pillar gets its own score from 0 to 100. Together, they become one final number.
Pillar one: Income

Earnings: the first brick

First, we look at how strong and dependable Aarav's income is. Not just how much he earns, but how steady the ground under it is.

Someone whose income is stable, or comes from more than one source, stands on firmer ground. Someone whose earnings swing up and down gets a more careful score.

What we look atThe level of income, how steady it is, and which way it's heading.
Pillar two: Expenses

Spending: where the story turns

Aarav earns well, yet his wallet is empty by the end of the month. This is where the Expenses pillar steps in. We look at how much of his income goes out the door, and whether that spending is under control.

Two people with the same salary can live completely different lives. One saves, the other borrows before the month ends. That's why spending is often the most honest mirror of all.

Living comfortably within your means pushes your score up.
Pillar three: Emergency Savings

Bad times don't send a warning

One day, news of layoffs hits Aarav's company. That night he understands what an emergency fund is for: the safety net that holds when everything else stops.

This pillar asks one question. If his income stopped tomorrow, how long could Aarav run his life calmly, without panic? The more breathing room, the better the score.

What we look atThe safe savings you've set aside, and how long they could carry your everyday life.
Pillar four: Protection

A shield for the unexpected

Aarav has savings. But could one major illness or accident undo years of hard work in a single blow? The Protection pillar exists to answer exactly that.

Here we look at how well Aarav and his family are covered through life and health insurance, and whether that cover truly matches the responsibilities he carries.

Building wealth is one skill. Keeping it safe is another.
Pillar five: Investment

Money that works for you

Saving alone isn't enough, because rising prices quietly shrink the value of idle money. Aarav's money has to go to work.

This pillar looks at whether Aarav invests regularly, and whether his money is spread across different places or sitting in a single basket. Steady, thoughtful investing counts the most here.

What we look atHow consistently you invest, how well it's spread out, and how close it keeps you to your goals.
Bringing it together

Five pillars become one number

Now each of Aarav's five pillars has its own score. MoneyMapper brings them together into a single Financial Fitness Score, and it's built so that one weak pillar can't hide behind a strong one.

If Aarav's income is excellent but his protection is almost nothing, the final score will show it plainly. That's how he knows exactly where to focus.

Below 40Needs attention
40 to 70Room to improve
Above 70Healthy

And it isn't a one-time verdict. As Aarav builds better habits, his score moves up month after month.
